tagline: A plateau loop reaches the meeting of rivers cut into volcanic rock.
intro: Wild Rivers Backcountry Byway loops across the sagebrush and piñon-juniper country of the Taos Plateau above a gorge cut through black rock. New Mexico’s tourism department presents the scenic byway as a way to reach the upper Rio Grande and its hiking, cycling and wildlife-viewing country. The paved approach continues beyond the end of state-maintained NM 378 onto BLM land. Volcanic cones, cliffs and the Sangre de Cristo peaks frame a landscape where the canyon falls 600 to 800 feet to the river.

Protection of the river preceded the national monument that surrounds this drive. In 1968, Congress included the Rio Grande among the first eight rivers in the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System. President Barack Obama proclaimed Rio Grande del Norte National Monument in 2013, encompassing the gorge and surrounding lands. Wild Rivers Recreation Area now lies within that monument, along protected reaches of both the Rio Grande and Red River.

From NM 522 north of Questa, turn west onto NM 378 and pass through Cerro. Continue onto the BLM road and into Wild Rivers Recreation Area. The loop passes the Wild Rivers Visitor Center and reaches La Junta Overlook, where the Red River meets the Rio Grande 800 feet below.

moments.title: Cerro
moments.text: Cerro takes its name from Cerro Guadalupe. Settlers from Taos and Questa founded the community in 1854. NM 378 passes through town heading west from NM 522, then ends at the boundary of BLM land. The pavement continues under another designation toward Wild Rivers Recreation Area.

moments.title: Wild Rivers Visitor Center
moments.text: A mural at the Wild Rivers Visitor Center is the work of a collaboration of New Mexico artists. The byway loop passes the center within Wild Rivers Recreation Area. The recreation area is part of Rio Grande del Norte National Monument, where the Rio Grande and Red River cut into volcanic flows. BLM manages the area through its Taos Field Office. Beyond the center, the recreation area includes overlooks, trails and campgrounds.

moments.title: La Junta Point
moments.text: At La Junta Point, the Red River meets the Rio Grande 800 feet below the rim. The overlook is wheelchair accessible. The Red River begins on the north slope of Mount Wheeler in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, flows west past Red River and Questa, then turns south into the Rio Grande. Here the two rivers have sliced into volcanic flows, exposing an 800-foot-deep canyon. Snowmelt and summer storms feed the Red River, whose relatively consistent mountain precipitation keeps it flowing throughout the year. The confluence lies just south of La Junta Campground.
moments.notice: The Red River joins the Rio Grande below the overlook.

practical: Wild Rivers Visitor Center: Expect daylight construction delays on roads within Wild Rivers Recreation Area. (checked 2026-10-11)
